title: Air pollution: dispersion, health burden, equity, and the footprint of the computation
text: individual area data confounders available, partially linear model Chernozhukov et al. (2018) estimates exposure effect cross-fitted nuisance functions, confounder adjustment overfit rows evaluated . exprspplr() adds percentile bootstrap sensitivity interval. default estimator uses ordinary-least-squares nuisances; estimator interface can passed. true coefficient 0.3 interval covers .
code: set.seed(1) n <- 300 sim <- data.frame(income = rnorm(n), density = rnorm(n)) sim$no2 <- 20 - 2 * sim$income + 3 * sim$density + rnorm(n) sim$asthmarate <- 5 + 0.3 * sim$no2 - 0.5 * sim$income + rnorm(n) fit <- exprspplr(sim, y = "asthmarate", expo = "no2",                              confs = c("income", "density"), nboot = 30) c(ate = fit$ate, lower = fit$cilobs, upper = fit$ciupbs) #>       ate     lower     upper  #> 0.2464713 0.1437978 0.3132657

title: Banded tables and concentration: from '6 to 10' to a Gini
text: Gini coefficient measures unequally total spread across units: 0 every unit holds , approaching 1 one unit holds everything. topshr() reports frequent account , lorenzc() gives curve behind Gini. top 1% people account disproportionate share placements: substantive finding banded table hides.
code: ginicoef(rep(1, 10))             # no concentration #> ╭── Gini coefficient ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Gini coefficient  0                                                       │ #> │   Units             10                                                      │ #> │   Total             10                                                      │ #> │   Largest unit      1 (10.0% of the total)                                  │ #> │   Most for n units  0.9                                                     │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   A Gini of 0: the total is close to equal shares.                          │ #> │   That is 0% of the way from equal shares (0) to one unit holding all of    │ #> │   it (0.9 for 10 units).                                                    │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   0 when every unit holds the same, 1 - 1/n when one unit holds it all;     │ #> │   doubling every value leaves it unchanged. It says how unequal, not        │ #> │   which units: topshr() and lorenzc() show where the total sits.            │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ ginicoef(c(rep(0, 9), 1))        # one unit holds everything #> ╭── Gini coefficient ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Gini coefficient  0.9                                                     │ #> │   Units             10                                                      │ #> │   Total             1                                                       │ #> │   Largest unit      1 (100.0% of the total)                                 │ #> │   Most for n units  0.9                                                     │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   A Gini of 0.9: the total is very highly concentrated.                     │ #> │   That is 100% of the way from equal shares (0) to one unit holding all of  │ #> │   it (0.9 for 10 units).                                                    │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   0 when every unit holds the same, 1 - 1/n when one unit holds it all;     │ #> │   doubling every value leaves it unchanged. It says how unequal, not        │ #> │   which units: topshr() and lorenzc() show where the total sits.            │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ 1 - 1 / 10                   # the maximum for ten units #> [1] 0.9  placements <- c(rep(1, 1200), rep(3, 430), rep(8, 110), rep(20, 38)) ginicoef(placements) #> ╭── Gini coefficient ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Gini coefficient  0.4612                                                  │ #> │   Units             1,778                                                   │ #> │   Total             4,130                                                   │ #> │   Largest unit      20 (0.5% of the total)                                  │ #> │   Most for n units  0.9994                                                  │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   A Gini of 0.4612: the total is highly concentrated.                       │ #> │   That is 46% of the way from equal shares (0) to one unit holding all of   │ #> │   it (0.9994 for 1,778 units).                                              │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   0 when every unit holds the same, 1 - 1/n when one unit holds it all;     │ #> │   doubling every value leaves it unchanged. title: Building reproducible data capsules
text: Everything starts data_provenance.json file: machine-readable pin project’s data source. records portal endpoint, pattern identifying right resource, expected SHA256, schema data must satisfy, recipe synthesizing stand-.
code: ckan <- paste0(   "https://data.ontario.ca/api/3/action/package_show",   "?id=ontario-public-library-statistics" ) provjson <- '{   "dataset": {     "title": "Demo library statistics",     "ckan_api_endpoint": "CKAN"   },   "resource": { "name_match_pattern": "2014" },   "schema": {     "expected_columns": ["year", "visits", "alert"],     "structural_invariants": { "min_data_rows": 5 },     "expected_value_sets": { "year": [2024, 2025] },     "synthetic_recipe": {       "n_rows": 25,       "seed": 42,       "columns": {         "year":   { "type": "sample",    "values": [2024, 2025] },         "visits": { "type": "poisson",   "lambda": 3, "min": 1 },         "alert":  { "type": "bernoulli", "p": 0.2 },         "id":     { "type": "id_pattern", "pattern": "p-{seq:05d}" }       }     }   } }' provjson <- sub("CKAN", ckan, provjson, fixed = TRUE)  provpath <- file.path(tempdir(), "data_provenance.json") writeLines(provjson, provpath)  prov <- loadprov(provpath) prov$dataset$title #> [1] "Demo library statistics"

title: Building reproducible data capsules
text: Every file gets SHA256; every data frame checked pinned schema. valsch() reports issues without raising, callers choose severity response; schval() strict wrapper (fatal issues stop, drift warns).
code: digest <- sha256file(datapath) substr(digest, 1, 16) #> [1] "e2f4b6752a2e3b56"  chk <- vrfsha256(datapath, digest) chk$match #> [1] TRUE  issues <- valsch(df, prov) length(issues)   # 0 = clean against the pinned schema #> [1] 0

title: Building reproducible data capsules
text: mkmnf() + recrd() accumulate named cross-checks (PASS / DIFFER / INFO), writers produce two capsule artifacts: machine-readable manifest.json human-readable SUMMARY.txt. capsule directory now contains everything reviewer needs trace run: exact inputs, digests, every cross-check status, plain-language account — reproducible years later even portal moved .
code: man <- mkmnf(   list(project = "demo-study", author = "A. Author", synthetic = TRUE),   env = FALSE  # TRUE also snapshots R/OS/package versions )  man <- recrd(man, "rowsgenerated", obs = gen$rows, expd = 25) #>   rowsgenerated                                observed = 25.0000      expected = 25.0000      [INFO] man <- recrd(man, "meanvisits",               obs = mean(df$visits), expd = 3,               tol = 1, syn = TRUE) #>   meanvisits                                   observed = 2.8000       expected = 3.0000       [INFO]  outdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "capsule-demo") dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE)  wrmnfjs(man, file.path(outdir, "manifest.json")) summarypath <- wrsmrytxt(   man, outdir,   paths = list(input = datapath, results = outdir),   whatwasdone = c("* generated synthetic stand-in (real source offline)",                     "* validated schema and recorded cross-checks") )  cat(readLines(summarypath)[7:12], sep = "\n") #> Project:   demo-study #> Author:    A. Author #> When:      2026-10-29 17:40:39 UTC #> OS:        Linux #> R:         R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24) #> Mode:      SYNTHETIC (not real data -- pipeline check only)

what: Do incidents repeat nearby, soon after? The Knox test
title: Courts and crime: flow, time, outcomes, place and case mix
text: Break-ins close space time earlier one near-repeat pattern. Knox test compares pairs close number expected dates shuffled among places; expectation exact, permutation test gives cell’s p-value.
code: b <- b[!is.na(b$lon), ] kn <- knoxtst(b$lon, b$lat, as.Date(b$occ_date), spcbands = c(100, 200, 400),                 tmbands = c(7, 14, 28), nsim = 199, seed = 1) kn #> ╭── Knox test of near-repeat incidents ───────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Incidents     508                                                         │ #> │   Permutations  199                                                         │ #> │   Close pairs   5,585                                                       │ #> │   Space bands   100, 200, 400                                               │ #> │   Time bands    7, 14, 28                                                   │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   Knox ratios, observed / expected pairs                                    │ #> │   distance   0-7 d   7-14 d  14-28 d                                        │ #> │   ---------  ------  ------  -------                                        │ #> │   0-100 m    1.66**  1.16    1.09                                           │ #> │   100-200 m  1.25    0.91    1.17                                           │ #> │   200-400 m  1.07    1.03    1.01                                           │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   A ratio above 1: more pairs this close in space and in time than          │ #> │   chance alone gives, the near-repeat pattern.                              │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, one-sided per cell (not adjusted for the number  │ #> │   of cells); - nothing expected                                             │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ plot(kn)

title: Hawkes processes: self-exciting event series
text: Ogata’s thinning algorithm simulates process exactly: propose events upper bound intensity keep probability λ(t)/λmax\lambda(t)/\lambda_{\max}. exponential kernel ϕ(s)=αβe−βs\phi(s) = \alpha \beta e^{-\beta s}, whose branching ratio α\alpha:
code: simhwk <- function(mu, alpha, beta, horizon, seed = 1) {   set.seed(seed)   t <- 0   events <- numeric(0)   while (t < horizon) {     lambdamax <- mu + alpha * beta * sum(exp(-beta * (t - events)))     t <- t + stats::rexp(1, lambdamax)     if (t >= horizon) break     lambdat <- mu + alpha * beta * sum(exp(-beta * (t - events)))     if (stats::runif(1) <= lambdat / lambdamax) events <- c(events, t)   }   events } times <- simhwk(mu = 1, alpha = 0.5, beta = 2, horizon = 300) length(times) #> [1] 559

text: Published applications designs often share weaknesses, remedy . clusters. reform assigned handful districts gives cluster-robust tests reject often. wcb() gives honest p-value interval; four clusters says plainly nothing can rejected 5%: Doubts parallel trends. tse() asks large departure parallel trends, relative largest seen adoption, make effect vanish: Covariates differ groups. stgatt() covs doubly robust (use covariates fixed treatment: one reform moves, arrests, bad control). plndml() lets machine learner fit confounding fixed effects, mtchdid() matches units pre-reform paths differencing: single treated place, . syndid() weights comparison units pre-periods:  Null results without measure power. plnpwr() simulates design untreated data gives minimum detectable effect:

title: Evaluating a policy from administrative panels
text: Every estimator takes data frame one row per unit period names columns, data need layout. eight towns ten years, four adopting -law (two 2019, two 2021), typed : arguments name columns: unit time: unit ("town") period, number ("year"; month index date turned number works ); y: outcome ("rate"); treatment, one two forms: trtd, 0/1 column 1 periods unit treated ("bylaw", plndid(), wcb(), bacondcmp(), swtdid(), loounit()), ftreat, period unit first treated, NA unit never treated ("first", evstudy(), stgatt(), perminf(), mtchdid(), syndid(), cohtrnd()); covs: covariate columns ("income"); cl: cluster column standard errors (default unit; "county" -law assigned county); w: weight column ("pop"), conflvl confidence level. 1. Look first. cohort’s outcome around adoption:  2. effect. two-way fixed-effects estimate, income control, weighted population, 90% level: 3. Period period. event study, sensitivity parallel trends:  4. Staggered adoption. cohort towns yet treated: 5. Honest inference clusters. eight towns, wild cluster bootstrap permutation test:

code: set.seed(1) n <- 600 d <- data.frame(   region = sample(c("north", "south", "east"), n, replace = TRUE),   age = sample(c("15-24", "25-49", "50+"), n, replace = TRUE),   used = rbinom(n, 1, 0.3),   drinks = rpois(n, 3),   w = runif(n, 40, 160) ) # a stratified design: variance by linearization lin <- svydes(d, w = "w", strata = "region") lin #> ╭── Survey design ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Respondents         600                                               │ #> │   Sum of weights      60,110                                            │ #> │   Variance            Taylor linearization                              │ #> │   Strata              3                                                 │ #> │   PSUs                600                                               │ #> │   Lonely PSUs         fail                                              │ #> │   Degrees of freedom  597                                               │ #> │                                                                         │ #> │   svyest() and svycmp() use this design for every estimate: the weights │ #> │   for the point estimate, the strata and PSUs for its standard error.   │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ # a replicate design: 200 bootstrap weights, made here by resampling within # region reps <- vapply(1:200, function(r) {   m <- numeric(n)   for (g in unique(d$region)) {     i <- which(d$region == g)     m[i] <- tabulate(sample(length(i), replace = TRUE), length(i)) *       length(i) /       (length(i) - 1)   }   d$w * m }, numeric(n)) repdes <- svydes(d, w = "w", reps = reps, type = "bootstrap") repdes #> ╭── Survey design ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Respondents         600                                               │ #> │   Sum of weights      60,110                                            │ #> │   Variance            bootstrap replicate weights                       │ #> │   Replicates          200                                               │ #> │   Scale               0.005                                             │ #> │   Centring            on the full-sample estimate                       │ #> │   Lonely PSUs         fail                                              │ #> │   Degrees of freedom  199                                               │ #> │                                                                         │ #> │   svyest() and svycmp() use this design for every estimate: the weights │ #> │   for the point estimate, the replicate weights for its standard error. │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

code: library(rmoriebricklayer) otis <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "otis_a01_individuals.csv",                              package = "rmoriebricklayer")) a <- anltab(otis, value = "individuals", prd = "year",             by = c("table", "group"), rnd = 5) a                                   # what changed, how sure, what was withheld rptanl(a, file.path(tempdir(), "otis.html"))   # one self-contained file library(rmoriebricklayer)  # 1. The pin: portal endpoint, resource pattern, expected schema, recipe. prov_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "data_provenance.json") writeLines('{   "dataset": {     "title": "Demo library statistics",     "ckan_api_endpoint": "https://data.ontario.ca/api/3/action/package_show?id=ontario-public-library-statistics"   },   "resource": { "name_match_pattern": "2014" },   "schema": {     "expected_columns": ["year", "visits", "alert"],     "structural_invariants": { "min_data_rows": 5 },     "expected_value_sets": { "year": [2024, 2025] },     "synthetic_recipe": {       "n_rows": 25, "seed": 42,       "columns": {         "year":   { "type": "sample",    "values": [2024, 2025] },         "visits": { "type": "poisson",   "lambda": 3, "min": 1 },         "alert":  { "type": "bernoulli", "p": 0.2 },         "id":     { "type": "id_pattern", "pattern": "p-{seq:05d}" }       }     }   } }', prov_path) prov <- loadprov(prov_path)  # 2. The data. With network: resolve the pinned endpoint to a current URL and #    download (Wayback fallback). Without: a reproducible stand-in from the #    recipe, marked synthetic all the way through. #   url  <- rslvckan(prov) #   path <- fdl(url, file.path(tempdir(), "data.csv")) path <- file.path(tempdir(), "data.csv") gen  <- mksyncsv(prov$schema$synthetic_recipe, path)  # 3. Integrity and schema. sha256file(path)                               # pin this in the provenance df     <- read.csv(path) issues <- valsch(df, prov)             # names, types, value sets, rows  # 4. The manifest: named cross-checks, then the two capsule artifacts. man <- mkmnf(list(project = "my-study", synthetic = TRUE)) man <- recrd(man, "rows", obs = nrow(df), expd = gen$rows, syn = TRUE) wrmnfjs(man, file.path(tempdir(), "manifest.json")) wrsmrytxt(man, tempdir(),                   paths = list(input = path, results = tempdir()),                   whatwasdone = "* validated the schema and recorded the row count") # Did the distribution change, not just the bytes? set.seed(1) ref  <- data.frame(value = rnorm(300), size = runif(300, 1, 10),                    grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 300, TRUE)) same <- data.frame(value = rnorm(300), size = runif(300, 1, 10),                    grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 300, TRUE)) cpsdrft(ref, same)$anydrft          # a fresh draw: FALSE moved <- same moved$size <- moved$size * 3              # a silently rescaled column moved$grade[1:100] <- "z"                 # and a new category cpsdrft(ref, moved)                 # both are caught  # Authenticate the manifest so a verifier knows who produced it. digest <- sha256file(file.path(tempdir(), "manifest.json")) key <- fipskg()                      # SLH-DSA: rests on the hash alone sig <- cpssign(digest, key) cpsvrf(digest, sig, fipspubkey(key)) cpsxvrf(digest, sig, fipspubkey(key)) # and again with OpenSSL 3.5 mod <- fipsmod()                     # the module and its certificate key <- fipsmkg("ML-DSA-65", mod)     # the private key never leaves it sig <- cpssign(digest, key) cpsvrf(digest, sig, key)

`help start`, `help llm`, `help config`, `help r` rmoriebricklayer doctor                         # which routes answer here, and the one ask will use rmoriebricklayer ask "your question"            # own endpoint, a provider with a key, then Ollama rmoriebricklayer ask --model NAME "your question" rmoriebricklayer ask --route anthropic "your question"   # one route, this time rmoriebricklayer aye "your question"            # aye and tellme are ask under other names rmoriebricklayer tellme "your question" rmoriebricklayer config                         # every language-model setting and where it comes from rmoriebricklayer config setup                   # pick a provider, paste its key, pick a model rmoriebricklayer config set route anthropic     # always this provider rmoriebricklayer config set anthropic.key       # asks for the key; saved privately rmoriebricklayer config set ollama.url http://192.168.1.20:11434 rmoriebricklayer config set own.url http://localhost:1234/v1 rmoriebricklayer config unset route             # back to the automatic order rmoriebricklayer config reset --force           # move an unreadable settings file aside rmoriebricklayer explain-error "the error text" # where an error comes from, no model needed rmoriebricklayer models --route ollama          # the models a route offers, the one in use marked rmoriebricklayer login --token                  # the data key: paste the key you were issued rmoriebricklayer login --email you@example.com  # or: a code is emailed, type it at the prompt rmoriebricklayer login --email you@example.com --code 123456   # the same, code passed (scripts) rmoriebricklayer login                          # or: GitHub device flow rmoriebricklayer login --no-browser             # server / SSH: prints a link + code for any device rmoriebricklayer logout                         # forget the data key rmoriebricklayer data list                      # the curated tables at data.rmorie.com rmoriebricklayer data pull db/table --out t.csv # download one (your MORIE key) rmoriebricklayer app [PATH]                     # the analysis dashboard (needs shiny) rmoriebricklayer wayback urls.txt --out w.jsonl # archive every URL in a file (archive.org keys) rmoriebricklayer wayback --retry w.jsonl        # retry the ones that failed rmoriebricklayer archive save URL --reason TEXT # save from this connection to archive.rmorie.com rmoriebricklayer archive find URL               # its captures; archive get ID -o FILE fetches one rmoriebricklayer pack --new my-study            # start a reproducibility bundle project (mkbndlproj()) rmoriebricklayer pack my-study --data data.csv  # its zip, data inside; a reviewer double-clicks it (mkbndl()) rmoriebricklayer bundle "your request"          # agentbndl() from the shell rmoriebricklayer verify capsules --fail-on warn # every capsule under a folder, as the rmbl GitHub Action checks it rmoriebricklayer verify capsules --json         # the check rows as JSON (hmac secret: RMBL_KEY) rmoriebricklayer drift capsules                 # fetch each source again and compare it with the pin rmoriebricklayer drift capsules --psi-warn 0.1 --psi-fail 0.25   # the PSI bands of the column table rmoriebricklayer drift capsules --allow-file --cache .rmbl-cache --snapshot   # file:// sources, a cache, snapshots rmoriebricklayer verify capsules --base base-copy/   # each manifest against its base copy (a file or a folder) rmoriebricklayer refresh capsules               # pin each source's new bytes (cpsrfrsh()) RMBL_KEY=... rmoriebricklayer sign capsules     # pin each plain provenance and sign each capsule (cpsseal()) rmoriebricklayer sign capsules --scheme ML-DSA-44 --key-file key.json --overwrite rmoriebricklayer report capsules --format md    # the Markdown report; never fails rmoriebricklayer functions [PATTERN]            # exported functions and their titles rmoriebricklayer describe NAME                  # one function's help page rmoriebricklayer examples NAME                  # its examples rmoriebricklayer version rmbl help rmbl doctor rmbl config setup rmbl ask "your question" rmbl aye "your question" rmbl tellme "your question" rmbl "how do I weight a survey?"               # a quoted question with no verb is asked too rmbl login --token rmbl models

title: Population attributable fraction — attrfrac
text: Levin's formula (Levin 1953; Rothman, Greenland Lash 2008, chapter 5): $$PAF = p (RR - 1) / (1 + p (RR - 1)),$$ \(p\) proportion exposed. everyone exposed \(1 - 1/RR\). assumes relative risk causal unconfounded removing exposure changes nothing else. relative risk 1 gives negative fraction (exposure protects). confidence limits RR given, fraction's limits formula applied : formula increases RR, interval fraction image interval risk. Refusals: rr limit single finite positive number (logical values included), prevalence outside \([0, 1]\), one two limits, limits enclose rr.

title: Base64 encoding — b64
text: jsb64enc() breaks output 72-character lines (newline complete block 54 input bytes), matching jsonlite's encoder byte byte; decoder ignores line breaks, white space = padding, either form round trips. character outside alphabet error rather skipped, skipping decode corrupted body shorter valid-looking one. URL-safe variant substitutes - _ + / drops = padding, makes safe URL path, query string filename. Base64 ENCODING, encryption digest: hides nothing anyone can reverse . Use csha256() pin content chmac() authenticate . Errors: encoder given anything raw vector, character vector NULL; jsb64dec() given anything text raw bytes, text character outside standard alphabet; jsb64udec() given anything character text (raw bytes refused), NA, character outside URL-safe alphabet.

title: Base64 encoding — b64
code: # Round trip through the standard alphabet. b <- jsb64enc("hello capsule") b #> [1] "aGVsbG8gY2Fwc3VsZQ==" rawToChar(jsb64dec(b)) #> [1] "hello capsule"  # Raw input works the same way. jsb64enc(charToRaw("abc")) #> [1] "YWJj" jsb64dec(jsb64enc(charToRaw("abc"))) #> [1] 61 62 63  # Padding appears when the length is not a multiple of three. jsb64enc("a") #> [1] "YQ==" jsb64enc("ab") #> [1] "YWI=" jsb64enc("abc") #> [1] "YWJj"  # The URL-safe variant has no "+", "/" or "=" to escape. jsb64uenc(as.raw(c(255, 224, 63))) #> [1] "_-A_" jsb64enc(as.raw(c(255, 224, 63))) #> [1] "/+A/" jsb64udec(   jsb64uenc("path/safe?yes") ) #>  [1] 70 61 74 68 2f 73 61 66 65 3f 79 65 73  # Long input is wrapped, and the decoder ignores the breaks. long <- jsb64enc(strrep("x", 200)) grepl("\n", long) #> [1] TRUE rawToChar(jsb64dec(long)) == strrep("x", 200) #> [1] TRUE  # A character outside the alphabet is refused, not skipped. try(jsb64dec("ab$c")) #> Error : base64 input contains characters outside the alphabet

title: Hawkes-process negative log-likelihood (C backend) — chwknll
text:
Four triggering kernels available. "exponential" memoryless evaluates O(n) recursion; three , cost O(n^2). Parameters passed scales kernel defined : par = c(a0, eta, ...) a0 LOG baseline intensity ( \(
u = e^{a0}\)) eta branching ratio (0, 1) – expected number children per event, process stationary eta < 1. remaining entries kernel's shape parameters: beta (exponential), alpha, lambda (Weibull: shape scale), alpha, c (Lomax: shape scale, \(g(u) = \alpha c^\alpha (u + c)^{-(\alpha + 1)}\)), alpha, beta (gamma: shape rate). likelihood chwkfit() maximises, parameters. conditional intensity \(\lambda(t) = 
u + \eta \sum_{t_i < t} g(t - t_i)\) \(g\) probability density \((0, \infty)\) (\(\eta\) branching ratio), value returned $$-\ell = -\sum_i \log \lambda(t_i) + \int_0^T \lambda(t)\,dt,$$ \(T\) = hor (Hawkes, 1971). exponential kernel \(g(u) =  eta e^{- eta u}\). events value compensator alone, \(
u T\). feasible region, outside sentinel 1e12 returned instead value: \(-20 < a_0 < 20\); \(10^{-6} < \eta < 0.999\); kernel parameters, exponential \(0.05 \le  eta \le 30\); Weibull shape \([0.05, 20]\) scale \([0.001, 1000]\); Lomax shape \([0.05, 30]\) scale \([0.001, 100]\); gamma shape \([0.05, 20]\) rate \([0.05, 30]\). missing parameter also gives sentinel. Refusals (errors, sentinel): times missing value, sorted, outside \([0, T]\); hor single positive finite number; kernel among four; par wrong length kernel. quadratic kernels poll Ctrl-C run, long evaluation can interrupted.

title: Hawkes-process negative log-likelihood (C backend) — chwknll

title: Hawkes-process negative log-likelihood (C backend) — chwknll
code: set.seed(4) times <- sort(stats::runif(40, 0, 10))  # Exponential kernel: log-baseline -0.5, branching 0.3, decay 1.2. chwknll(times, 10, "exponential", c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.2)) #> [1] -1.8753  # Lower is better, so this is what an optimiser minimises. nll <- function(p) chwknll(times, 10, "exponential", p) fit <- stats::optim(c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.2), nll) fit$par #> [1] 1.03407757 0.99899989 0.08854609  # A branching ratio at or above 1 is not a stationary process, and is # reported as the infeasible sentinel rather than a number. chwknll(times, 10, "exponential", c(-0.5, 1.5, 1.2)) == 1e12 #> [1] TRUE  # The heavier-tailed kernels take two shape parameters. chwknll(times, 10, "gamma", c(-0.5, 0.3, 2, 1.5)) #> [1] -1.550628  # Unsorted times are an error, not the sentinel. try(chwknll(rev(times), 10, "exponential", c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.2))) #> Error : chwknll: `times` must be sorted in increasing order

title: Trimmed inverse-probability weights (C backend) — cipw
text: unit \(\) treatment \(T_i\) propensity \(e_i\), clamped score \(\tilde e_i = \min(\max(e_i, l), u)\) \(l\) = trimlo \(u\) = trimhi, weight \(1 / \tilde e_i\) \(T_i = 1\) \(1 / (1 - \tilde e_i)\) \(T_i = 0\). defaults weight exceeds 100. Refusals: vectors different lengths, treatment coded 0/1 ("treat must coded 0/1", naming offending values), propensity outside \([0, 1]\), bounds satisfy \(0 < l < u < 1\). missing treatment propensity gives missing weight unit . weights normalised; divide sum within arm stabilised (Hajek) estimates.

text: ginicoef(): numeric scalar [0, 1 - 1/n]. lorenzc(): data frame numeric columns population (cumulative share units, 0 1) value (cumulative share total, units ascending order), n + 1 rows including origin. topshr(): data frame columns fraction (requested fraction units), units (many largest units fraction ) share (share total units hold). class c("rmbl_gini", "rmbl_measure", "numeric"), prints box inputs (kept attribute "lakner"); arithmetic, [, c() .numeric() give plain numbers.

title: Concentration of a total across units — concentration
text: Gini mean absolute difference pairs units twice mean, \(G = \sum_i \sum_j |x_i - x_j| / (2 n^2 \bar{x})\), also twice area Lorenz curve diagonal. Zero perfectly even spread; maximum n units 1 - 1/n, 1, Gini near 1 requires many units well uneven spread. Gini computed banded rounded data inherits coarsening: compare bandsens() values bands. tail units dominate, hilltlidx() says whether largest values follow power law. Errors: x numeric, Inf negative value, non-missing value; ginicoef() every value zero (Gini zero total undefined); topshr() fractions numeric, empty, NA lies outside [0, 1].

a correlation is blank when too few pairs remain.     │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # Pearson instead of Spearman cortbl(df, meth = "pearson") #> ╭── Correlations (pearson) ───────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Method         pearson                                                │ #> │   Pairs          3                                                      │ #> │   Strongest |r|  0.9747                                                 │ #> │                                                                         │ #> │   x  y  correlation  nprs                                               │ #> │   -  -  -----------  ----                                               │ #> │   a  b      -0.0010   100                                               │ #> │   a  c       0.9747   100                                               │ #> │   b  c      -0.0120   100                                               │ #> │                                                                         │ #> │   Each row is one pair of numeric columns, over the rows where both are │ #> │   present (nprs); a correlation is blank when too few pairs remain.     │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # nprs shows how much data each figure rests on. gappy <- df gappy$a[1:80] <- NA cortbl(gappy) #> ╭── Correlations (spearman) ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Method         Spearman (rank)                                        │ #> │   Pairs          3                                                      │ #> │   Strongest |r|  0.9594                                                 │ #> │                                                                         │ #> │   x  y  correlation  nprs                                               │ #> │   -  -  -----------  ----                                               │ #> │   a  b        0.165    20                                               │ #> │   a  c        0.959    20                                               │ #> │   b  c        0.015   100                                               │ #> │                                                                         │ #> │   Each row is one pair of numeric columns, over the rows where both are │ #> │   present (nprs); a correlation is blank when too few pairs remain.     │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # A pair with too little overlap is NA, not a number from nothing. thin <- df thin$a[1:99] <- NA cortbl(thin)$correlation #> [1]         NA         NA 0.01508551  # one numeric column cannot be correlated try(cortbl(data.frame(a = 1:5, b = letters[1:5]))) #> Error : cortbl: need at least two numeric columns to correlate

title: Attest a capsule, binding a signature to what it covers — cpsatst
text: man manifest, mkmnf(). key cpsatst(), signing key fipskg() (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA standardised schemes) pqckg() (XMSS), shared secret (string raw vector) "hmac". cpschkatst(), shared secret checks "hmac" attestation; used schemes, whose public key attestation carries. ctx Optional context string (raw vector), bound signature standardised schemes; see cpssign(). NULL (default) means none. prehash Pre-hash, cpssign(). "none" (default) hash name "sha256" "sha512". note Optional free text recorded attestation – signature meant assert, signer's words. covered signature, since part digest. attest attestation cpsatst(). keyexp Optional public key attestation must carry, hex key object fipskg(), fipspubkey() signpubkey(). Supply know key signed: without check confirms attestation internally consistent, key's holder arrange.

title: Attest a capsule, binding a signature to what it covers — cpsatst
text: cpsatst() list class bricklayer_attestation character fields digest, scheme, public (hex), context, prehash, note signed_utc (ISO 8601 UTC time), signature (bricklayer_signature cpssign()). cpschkatst() list class bricklayer_attestation_check ok (logical) checks, data frame columns check, ok detail, one row per check.

title: Attest a capsule, binding a signature to what it covers — cpsatst
text: adds cpssign(). bare signature leaves three things implicit – key, scheme, bytes. verifier told band check anything already given, makes signature formality. attestation states , check cpschkatst(attestation, manifest) nothing else. signed: payload digest (mnfdgst() manifest), scheme, public, ctx (hex raw context), prehash, note signed_utc put canonical form (mnfcanon()) SHA-256 signed cpssign(). Every field, note time included, therefore covered: editing breaks signature. XMSS key pqckg() scheme "xmss-sha256" context pre-hash used signature; signing uses one key's one-time indices, every XMSS signature . shared secret (string raw vector) key scheme "hmac": HMAC-SHA-256 secret, cpssign(scheme = "hmac"). public key id, hex HMAC-SHA-256 string "public" secret: names key, keyexp can pin , without revealing . secret never recorded, checking needs (key cpschkatst()). context "" prehash "none", bytes morie's capsule signer writes. HMAC symmetric: anyone can check signature can also make one. one post-quantum signature schemes carries none guarantees. check, one row : attestation_complete (every field present), manifest_digest (manifest's digest equals attested one), key_as_expected (keyexp given) signature (signature verifies attested public key; "hmac", key, whose key id must equal public). ok TRUE every row passes. establish. public key belongs whoever think : attestation good channel key arrived , keyexp exists. manifest true – changed since signed. cpsfals() question. chain seal recorded; attest run history, sign chnseal() directly. Errors: man list; key fipskg() pqckg() non-empty string raw vector; invalid prehash ctx (cpssign()), either given HMAC key; attestation cpsatst(). signature fails verify failed row, error.

title: Attest a capsule, binding a signature to what it covers — cpsatst
code: m <- mkmnf(list(dataset = "otis", rows = 1200L), env = FALSE) key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-65") att <- cpsatst(m, key, note = "counts as published") att #> ╭── Capsule attestation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Scheme           ML-DSA-65                                                │ #> │   Manifest digest  efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2 │ #> │                    bd0a9c90                                                 │ #> │   Context          <none>                                                   │ #> │   Prehash          none                                                     │ #> │   Note             counts as published                                      │ #> │   Signed           2026-10-29T17:38:24Z                                     │ #> │   Public key       5e387fad6f954784271ebda62f5c56a8... (1952 bytes)         │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   A signed claim that a manifest with this digest was attested by the       │ #> │   holder of the key; check it against the manifest with cpschkatst().       │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # a verifier needs the attestation and the manifest, nothing else res <- cpschkatst(att, m) res$ok #> [1] TRUE res$checks #>                  check   ok #> 1 attestation_complete TRUE #> 2      manifest_digest TRUE #> 3            signature TRUE #>                                                             detail #> 1                                                                  #> 2 efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2bd0a9c90 #> 3                                                                   # any change to the manifest breaks it m2 <- m m2$meta$rows <- 1201L cpschkatst(att, m2)$ok #> [1] FALSE  # and so does presenting a different key cpschkatst(att, m, keyexp = fipskg("ML-DSA-65")$public)$ok #> [1] FALSE  # the note is signed too: editing it breaks the signature row forged <- att forged$note <- "counts corrected" cpschkatst(forged, m)$checks[, c("check", "ok")] #>                  check    ok #> 1 attestation_complete  TRUE #> 2      manifest_digest  TRUE #> 3            signature FALSE  # a context string and a pre-hash att2 <- cpsatst(m, key, ctx = "release 2026-10", prehash = "sha512") cpschkatst(att2, m, keyexp = key)$ok #> [1] TRUE  # a shared secret signs with HMAC; `public` is its key id, not the secret att3 <- cpsatst(m, "shared-secret") att3$public #> [1] "4e289ef69cbe6f4c0d7de16c0801ad1155aba1598f2f4b25cddb46880caacd60" cpschkatst(att3, m, key = "shared-secret", keyexp = att3$public)$ok #> [1] TRUE cpschkatst(att3, m, key = "another-secret")$checks[, c(   "check",   "ok",   "detail" )] #>                  check    ok #> 1 attestation_complete  TRUE #> 2      manifest_digest  TRUE #> 3            signature FALSE #>                                                             detail #> 1                                                                  #> 2 efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2bd0a9c90 #> 3               the key given is not the key the attestation names  # a key that is not a signing key is refused try(cpsatst(m, 42)) #> Error : `key` must come from fipskg() or pqckg(), or be a shared secret (a string or raw vector) for hmac

code: dir <- tempfile() dir.create(dir) write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:3), file.path(dir, "data.csv"),           row.names = FALSE) m <- mkmnf(list(dataset = "demo"), env = FALSE) key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-44")  b <- cpsbndl(dir, m, key, note = "as published") cpsbndlvrf(attr(b, "path"), dir, man = m)$ok #> [1] TRUE  # touch a byte of the data and the bundle no longer holds write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:4), file.path(dir, "data.csv"),           row.names = FALSE) res <- cpsbndlvrf(attr(b, "path"), dir, man = m) res$ok #> [1] FALSE res$checks[!res$checks$ok, c("check", "detail")] #>           check #> 1 file:data.csv #>                                                                                                                                            detail #> 1 expected 95aecaa7399a39092c9e716ce1e18bb1c606c82f9503d679ac55c82988f6c38e, got 5140963bf019d514b126f382bc4c324b98109d2fd252c1858b60c821cff88c37  # read back, and checked against the key you expected to have signed b2 <- cpsbndlrd(attr(b, "path")) b2 #> ╭── Capsule bundle ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Files            1                                                        │ #> │   Manifest digest  8995763848bcf59327ed818c561d5428a958cd82f86a60c91e416796 │ #> │                    0781a579                                                 │ #> │   Bundled          2026-10-29T17:38:25Z                                     │ #> │   Scheme           ML-DSA-44                                                │ #> │   Note             as published                                             │ #> │   Path             /tmp/RtmptAMHMc/file1f8f61d10688/capsule_bundle.json     │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   A signed list of the capsule's files and their digests; check the files   │ #> │   against it with cpsbndlvrf().                                             │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯ cpsbndlvrf(b2, dir, keyexp = "00ff")$ok #> [1] FALSE  # a file added beside the bundle is reported too writeLines("x", file.path(dir, "extra.txt")) cpsbndlvrf(b2, dir)$checks[, c("check", "ok")] #>                              check    ok #> 1                    file:data.csv FALSE #> 2                no_unlisted_files FALSE #> 3 attestation:attestation_complete  TRUE #> 4      attestation:manifest_digest  TRUE #> 5            attestation:signature  TRUE  # a bundle signed with a shared secret (HMAC), as morie signs dir2 <- tempfile() dir.create(dir2) writeLines("x,y", file.path(dir2, "d.csv")) h <- cpsbndl(dir2, m, "shared-secret") h$attestation$public  # the key id, not the secret #> [1] "4e289ef69cbe6f4c0d7de16c0801ad1155aba1598f2f4b25cddb46880caacd60" cpsbndlvrf(attr(h, "path"), dir2, key = "shared-secret",            keyexp = h$attestation$public)$ok #> [1] TRUE # without the secret the signature row cannot pass cpsbndlvrf(attr(h, "path"), dir2)$ok #> [1] FALSE unlink(dir2, recursive = TRUE)  # a directory that does not exist try(cpsbndl(file.path(tempdir(), "no-such-capsule"), m, key)) #> Error : `dir` does not exist: /tmp/RtmptAMHMc/no-such-capsule unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)

code: set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(120), y = rnorm(120)) # inject a linear effect of x on y inj <- function(z, size) {   z$y <- z$y + size * z$x   z } pw <- cpspwr(d, function(z) cor(z$x, z$y), inj,                     sizes = c(0, 0.3, 0.6), trt = "x",                     n = 99, reps = 5, seed = 42) pw$curve #>   size detected reps rate #> 1  0.0        0    5    0 #> 2  0.3        5    5    1 #> 3  0.6        5    5    1 pw #> ╭── Positive controls: an injected effect of known size ──────────╮ #> │   Permutations          99                                      │ #> │   Repetitions per size  5                                       │ #> │   Alpha                 0.05                                    │ #> │   Treatment             x                                       │ #> │   False positive rate   0                                       │ #> │   Smallest detected     0.3                                     │ #> │                                                                 │ #> │     size  detected  rate                                        │ #> │   ------  --------  ----                                        │ #> │   0.0000  0/5          0                                        │ #> │   0.3000  5/5          1                                        │ #> │   0.6000  5/5          1                                        │ #> │                                                                 │ #> │   smallest size detected at a rate of 0.8: 0.3;                 │ #> │   a null result is informative only about effects at least this │ #> │   large; smaller ones would have been missed.                   │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # The rate at size 0 estimates the false-positive rate. With few # repetitions it is usually 0, because alpha is small -- five draws # at 0.05 come up empty about three times in four -- so read it as a # sanity check that it is not LARGE, not as an estimate of alpha. pw$curve[pw$curve$size == 0, "rate"] #> [1] 0  # an injection with fresh noise each time, and effects too small to be # detected in four repetitions: the smallest detected size is NA inj2 <- function(z, size) {   z$y <- z$y + size * z$x + stats::rnorm(nrow(z), sd = 0.5)   z } cpspwr(d, function(z) cor(z$x, z$y), inj2, sizes = c(0.1, 0.2),               trt = "x", n = 49, reps = 4, seed = 7)$smadet #> [1] NA  # too few permutations to ever reach alpha = 0.05 try(cpspwr(d, function(z) cor(z$x, z$y), inj, trt = "x", n = 9)) #> Error : with 9 permutations the smallest p-value is 0.1, which is above alpha = 0.05: no size could ever be detected

title: Quantiles, median and robust spread (C backend) — crob
text: x Numeric (logical) vector; coerced .numeric(). probs Numeric vector probabilities, \([0, 1]\) (default minimum, quartiles maximum). const Scale factor cmad(). default 1.4826 makes MAD consistent standard deviation normality, rounded value stats::mad() uses, two agree exactly. unrounded consistency constant 1 / qnorm(3/4) = 1.4826022185...; pass explicitly want extra digits, 1 unscaled median deviation. k Fence width IQRs, single non-negative number (default 1.5, Tukey's convention; 3 usual “far ” cutoff).

title: Quantiles, median and robust spread (C backend) — crob

title: Quantiles, median and robust spread (C backend) — crob
text: robust counterparts cmom(): single corrupted row can move mean variance arbitrarily far, moves median MAD hardly – want deciding whether freshly fetched column still column capsule pinned , screening column values inspect hand. type-7 quantile probability \(p\) interpolates linearly order statistics \(x_{(j)}\) \(x_{(j+1)}\) \(h = (n - 1)p + 1\), \(j = \lfloor h \rfloor\): \(Q(p) = x_{(j)} + (h - j)(x_{(j+1)} - x_{(j)})\) (Hyndman Fan, 1996). MAD \(c \cdot \mathrm{median}_i |x_i - \mathrm{median}(x)|\) \(c\) = constant; IQR \(Q(0.75) - Q(0.25)\); fences \(Q(0.25) - k \cdot \mathrm{IQR}\) \(Q(0.75) + k \cdot \mathrm{IQR}\) (Tukey, 1977). Missing values removed: NA NaN anywhere x makes every result NaN (unlike stats::quantile(), stops). empty x gives NaN. cqnt() refuses empty probs ("probs empty") probability outside \([0, 1]\) missing ("must lie [0, 1]"); every function refuses character, factor list x ("must numeric"). quantiles sort copy x, cost \(O(n \log n)\).

title: Quantiles, median and robust spread (C backend) — crob
code: x <- c(2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9) cqnt(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)) #> 25% 50% 75%  #> 4.0 4.5 5.5  all.equal(cqnt(x, c(0.1, 0.9)),           as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, c(0.1, 0.9)))) #> [1] "names for target but not for current"  cmed(x) #> [1] 4.5 cmad(x) #> [1] 0.7413 all.equal(cmad(x), stats::mad(x)) #> [1] TRUE cmad(x, const = 1)                  # unscaled median deviation #> [1] 0.5 cmad(x, const = 1 / stats::qnorm(3/4))  # unrounded constant #> [1] 0.7413011  ciqr(x) #> [1] 1.5 ctkyfnc(x) #> lower upper  #>  1.75  7.75   # Robustness: one wild value barely moves the median, but moves the # mean a long way. wild <- c(x, 1000) c(mean = mean(wild), median = cmed(wild)) #>     mean   median  #> 115.5556   5.0000   # Values outside the fences are the candidates to inspect. f <- ctkyfnc(wild) wild[wild < f[["lower"]] | wild > f[["upper"]]] #> [1] 1000  # A missing value is not dropped: the answer is NaN. cmed(c(1, NA, 3)) #> [1] NaN  # A probability outside [0, 1] is refused. try(cqnt(x, 1.5)) #> Error : `probs` must lie in [0, 1]

title: Weighted mean and variance (C backend) — cwtd
text: named length-2 numeric vector: mean (units x) variance (squared units x).

title: Weighted mean and variance (C backend) — cwtd
text: mean \(\bar x_w = \sum_i w_i x_i / \sum_i w_i\). weights treated RELIABILITY weights (precisely observation known), variance $$s_w^2 = \frac{\sum_i w_i (x_i - \bar x_w)^2}   {\sum_i w_i - \sum_i w_i^2 / \sum_i w_i},$$ unbiased estimator reading. every weight equal 1 reduces exactly stats::var(). Frequency weights (weight 3 meaning three identical rows) call denominator \(\sum w - 1\) instead, survey design weights call design-based variance, use variance . Refusals: x w different lengths ("must length"), negative weight ("must non-negative"), character, factor list argument ("must numeric"). -zero weights, NA either vector, give NaN entries.

title: Weighted mean and variance (C backend) — cwtd
code: x <- c(10, 20, 30, 40) w <- c(1, 1, 2, 4) cwtd(x, w) #>     mean variance  #>  31.2500 169.0476   # The mean agrees with base R. all.equal(cwtd(x, w)[["mean"]], stats::weighted.mean(x, w)) #> [1] TRUE  # Equal weights recover the unweighted variance. all.equal(cwtd(x, rep(1, 4))[["variance"]], stats::var(x)) #> [1] TRUE  # A single dominant weight pulls the mean onto that observation. cwtd(x, c(1, 1, 1, 1000))[["mean"]] #> [1] 39.94018  # A negative weight is refused. try(cwtd(x, c(1, -1, 1, 1))) #> Error : `w` must be non-negative and finite, not all zero

title: Download a File — dldata
text: url URL download, single string. tpath Destination path disk, single string. directory must exist. mode Kept signature utils::download.file(); "wb" (default) "w" accepted. Every transfer binary written fresh package's transport, append mode honoured error rather silent "wb". quiet Logical. TRUE suppresses progress output; FALSE (default) shows . allowfile Logical. title: Download a File — dldata
text: anything fetched URL must one public https URL: plain http needs option rmoriebricklayer.allowhttp set TRUE, file:// needs allowfile = TRUE, loopback, private, link-local cloud-metadata addresses refused. transport resolves host, pins connection checked addresses, re-checks every redirect hop, caps body 2 GiB allows 3600 seconds transfer. file tpath overwritten. Errors transfer (network, HTTP status, size cap) propagate R errors; nothing partial left behind. Progress drawn stderr quiet = FALSE, whatever morie.quiet option says, value passed transport explicitly. Errors: url tpath single non-empty string; refused URL; mode "wb" "w".

title: Download a File — dldata
code: # offline: a local file through a file:// URL src <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") writeLines(c("id,value", "1,10", "2,20"), src) dest <- dldata(paste0("file://", src), tempfile(fileext = ".csv"),   quiet = TRUE, allowfile = TRUE) read.csv(dest) #>   id value #> 1  1    10 #> 2  2    20  # file:// is refused unless asked for, and so is an append mode try(dldata(paste0("file://", src), tempfile())) #> Error : url must be an https:// URL, not file:// ('file:///tmp/RtmptAMHMc/file1f8f78844d3d.csv'); options(rmoriebricklayer.allowhttp = TRUE) admits a trusted plain-http mirror try(dldata("https://example.org/x.csv", tempfile(), mode = "a")) #> Error : `mode` must be "wb" (every transfer is binary) if (FALSE) { # interactive() # needs the network dest <- dldata("https://cloud.r-project.org/",   tempfile(fileext = ".html"),   quiet = TRUE ) file.exists(dest) }

code: key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-65") key$scheme #> [1] "ML-DSA-65"  sig <- cpssign("a manifest digest", key) cpsvrf("a manifest digest", sig, fipspubkey(key)) #> [1] TRUE  # A context string binds the signature to its purpose: the same # message signed for one context does not verify under another. sig2 <- cpssign("a manifest digest", key, ctx = "release") cpsvrf("a manifest digest", sig2, key, ctx = "release") #> [1] TRUE cpsvrf("a manifest digest", sig2, key, ctx = "staging") #> [1] FALSE  # A fixed seed reproduces the key (for test vectors only: a guessable # seed is a guessable key). seed <- as.raw(1:32) identical(fipskg("ML-DSA-44", seed)$public, fipskg("ML-DSA-44", seed)$public) #> [1] TRUE  # The public half carries no secret. names(fipspubkey(key)) #> [1] "public" "scheme"  # An unknown parameter set is refused. try(fipskg("ML-DSA-99")) #> Error : unknown scheme 'ML-DSA-99'. text: power law \(p(x) \propto x^{-\alpha}\) \(x_{min}\): discrete data, exact (default): log-likelihood zeta distribution truncated \(x_{min}\), \(-n \log \zeta(\alpha, x_{min}) - \alpha \sum \log x_i\), maximised \(\alpha\) \((1.0001, 25)\) stats::optimize(); \(\zeta\) hurwzeta(). standard error comes observed information, numerical second derivative. continuous data (discrete = FALSE): Hill estimator \(\hat\alpha = 1 + n / \sum \log(x_i / x_{min})\), standard error \((\hat\alpha - 1)/\sqrt{n}\). discrete data approx = TRUE: closed form \(x_{min} - 1/2\) place \(x_{min}\). ks Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance fitted distribution tail, computed per distinct value ties (counts ties) handled correctly. finite positive values x used; rest dropped silently. tail fewer mintl values, every tail value , alpha NA method says . estimate optimiser's bound flagged method reliable. Errors: positive finite value x; xmin single positive number (logical, factor text refused); discrete approx TRUE FALSE.

(local corpus; cited published paper.)

title: Tail index of a heavy-tailed count — hilltlidx
code: # A continuous Pareto tail with exponent 2.5. set.seed(1) x <- (1 - stats::runif(5000))^(-1 / 1.5) round(hilltlidx(x, xmin = 1, discrete = FALSE)$alpha, 2) #> [1] 2.49  # A discrete power law, where the exact likelihood is needed: the # closed-form correction is badly biased at a threshold of one. k <- 1:10000 p <- k^(-2.5) / sum(k^(-2.5)) set.seed(2) z <- sample(k, 5000, replace = TRUE, prob = p) c(exact = round(hilltlidx(z, xmin = 1)$alpha, 2),   approx = round(hilltlidx(z, xmin = 1, approx = TRUE)$alpha, 2)) #>  exact approx  #>   2.46   2.00   # A short tail still returns an estimate, marked as not to be leaned # on, and with a standard error that says the same thing. short <- hilltlidx(c(3, 4, 5, 9), xmin = 3) c(alpha = round(short$alpha, 2), n = short$ntl,   reliable = short$reliable) #>    alpha        n reliable  #>     2.59     4.00     0.00   # Below `mintl` there is nothing to estimate from. hilltlidx(c(3, 4), xmin = 3)$alpha #> [1] NA  # the threshold has to be positive try(hilltlidx(z, xmin = 0)) #> Error : `xmin` must be positive

code: key <- hqckg(1) pub <- hqcpubkey(key)  # the sender holds only the public key sent <- hqcencap(pub) # the recipient recovers the same secret from the ciphertext got <- hqcdecap(key, sent$ciphertext) identical(sent$shared, got) #> [1] TRUE  # a corrupted ciphertext yields a DIFFERENT secret, not an error bad <- sent$ciphertext substring(bad, 1L, 2L) <- if (substring(bad, 1L, 2L) == "00") "01" else "00" identical(hqcdecap(key, bad), got) #> [1] FALSE  # a reproducible key from a fixed seed identical(hqckg(1, seed = as.raw(1:32))$public,           hqckg(1, seed = as.raw(1:32))$public) #> [1] TRUE  # the round-4 revision: the same exchange, a 64-byte shared secret old <- hqckg(1, ver = "round4") cap <- hqcencap(hqcpubkey(old)) nchar(cap$shared) / 2 #> [1] 64 identical(hqcdecap(old, cap$ciphertext), cap$shared) #> [1] TRUE

code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   id = 1:100,   score = stats::runif(100, 0, 10),   grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 100, TRUE),   note = paste0("free text ", 1:100),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  sch <- infsch(df) sch #> ╭── Inferred schema ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Columns         4                                                         │ #> │   Rows            90 to 111                                                 │ #> │   Value sets      1                                                         │ #> │   Numeric ranges  2                                                         │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   What later extracts must look like to pass valsch(): these columns and    │ #> │   types, missingness at most as shown, values inside these sets.            │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   id                   integer    max NA  10.0%  [ -8.9, 109.9]             │ #> │   score                numeric    max NA  10.0%  [-0.8446,  10.9]           │ #> │   grade                character  max NA  10.0%  a, b, c                    │ #> │   note                 character  max NA  10.0%  – free                     │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # The categorical column has its levels pinned; the free-text one does # not, because it exceeds max_levels. sch$expected_value_sets #> $grade #> [1] "a" "b" "c" #>   # It validates the data it was learned from. length(valsch(df, list(schema = sch))) #> [1] 0  # And catches a column that has gone missing, or a new category. length(valsch(df[, -3], list(schema = sch))) > 0 #> [1] TRUE bad <- df; bad$grade[1] <- "z" length(valsch(bad, list(schema = sch))) > 0 #> [1] TRUE  # no slack pins the exact observed range infsch(df, slack = 0)$numeric_ranges$score #>       min       max  #> 0.1339033 9.9190609   # a negative slack is refused try(infsch(df, slack = -0.1)) #> Error : `slack` must be a single non-negative number, at most 100

Use payloads travel, plain tojs() anything person meant read git diff meant show. raw = TRUE skips base64 step returns gzip bytes, use writing file rather embedding text. bytes real gzip member (RFC 1952, header bytes 1f 8b), readable gzip -d, zcat HTTP client, zlib stream memCompress(type = "gzip") returns. modification time header zero, input always gives bytes digest result depend clock. base64 text uses standard alphabet line breaks every 72 characters (jsb64enc()). decoder takes input's type: raw vector read gzip bytes whatever raw says, text base64. guard decompression bombs refuses member whose declared uncompressed size 64 MiB. title: Compressed, base64-encoded JSON — jsgz
code: x <- list(rows = data.frame(id = 1:50, value = stats::runif(50)))  enc <- jsgzenc(x) substring(enc, 1, 40) #> [1] "H4sIAAAAAAAA/1XSTUoEMRAF4LtkPUj9ppK+irgQ"  # Smaller than the JSON it came from, because the keys repeat. c(json = nchar(tojs(x)), gzipb64 = nchar(enc)) #>    json gzipb64  #>    1244     429   # Round trips. identical(jsgzdec(enc)$rows$id, 1:50) #> [1] TRUE  # Raw gzip bytes, for writing to a file. bytes <- jsgzenc(x, raw = TRUE) class(bytes) #> [1] "raw" identical(jsgzdec(bytes, raw = TRUE)$rows$id, 1:50) #> [1] TRUE  # the bytes are ordinary gzip: a file any gzip tool can read f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json.gz") writeBin(bytes, f) substr(readLines(gzfile(f), warn = FALSE), 1, 40) #> [1] "{\"rows\":[{\"id\":1,\"value\":0.28},{\"id\":2,\""  # options pass through to the JSON writer and reader jsgzdec(jsgzenc(list(a = 1, b = "x"), auto_unbox = TRUE),                  simplifyVector = FALSE) #> $a #> [1] 1 #>  #> $b #> [1] "x" #>   # text that is not a gzip member is refused try(jsgzdec(jsb64enc("not gzip"))) #> Error : `txt` does not hold a gzip member: expected at least 18 bytes starting 1f 8b, got 8 byte(s).

title: JSON serialisation of an R object, type and attributes included — jsserdoc
code: # A factor survives the round trip with its levels intact. f <- factor(c("b", "a", "b"), levels = c("a", "b", "c")) back <- jsunser(jsser(f)) identical(back, f) #> [1] TRUE  # So does a matrix, with its dimensions. m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2) identical(jsunser(jsser(m)), m) #> [1] TRUE  # Plain data JSON does not keep either, which is the trade-off. tojs(f) #> ["b","a","b"]   # Nested lists, names and NULLs round trip too. x <- list(a = 1:3, b = list(c = "x", d = NULL), e = TRUE) identical(jsunser(jsser(x)), x) #> [1] TRUE  # Doubles are rounded to `digits`; I(17) keeps them exact. jsser(1/3) #> {"type":"double","attributes":{},"value":[0.33333333]}  exact <- jsser(1/3, digits = I(17)) identical(jsunser(exact), 1/3) #> [1] TRUE  # The serialised form is JSON, so it can be pinned like any other text. nchar(csha256(jsser(m))) #> [1] 64  # A function is refused unless the JSON is trusted. try(jsunser(jsser(function(x) x + 1))) #> Error : jsunser() refuses to rebuild a 'closure' from JSON it did not write: that would run code chosen by the file's author. Pass trusted = TRUE only for JSON produced by jsser() in your own session.

title: Search theory for search and rescue planning — ltrlrng
text: quantities search rescue planner works (Koopman's search theory, used U.S. Coast Guard IAMSAR planning methods): ltrlrng() (lateral range): probability sensor passing distance x detects object, inverse cube, definite range M-Beta model sweep width W; swpwdth() (sweep width): area sampled lateral range curve; srchpod() (search POD): probability detection coverage, random search, definite-range sweep inverse cube parallel sweep; pswppod() (parallel sweep POD): POD parallel sweep track spacing S, computed model, optional normal navigation error; srchscs() (search success): probability success, cumulative POD repeated searches containment probabilities updated unsuccessful search; datumpmap() (datum probability map): probability grid cell contains object, point, line area datum; optcrcsrch() (optimal circular search): Koopman's optimal effort circular normal datum; opteffort() (optimal effort): allocation fixed effort cells maximises probability success.

title: Search theory for search and rescue planning — ltrlrng
code: ltrlrng(x, W, model = c("invcube", "definite", "mbeta"), m = 1, navsd = 0)  swpwdth(x, p = NULL)  srchpod(   coverage = NULL,   model = c("random", "definite", "invcube", "mbeta"),   m = 1,   W = NULL,   effort = NULL,   area = NULL )  pswppod(   W,   S,   model = c("invcube", "definite", "mbeta"),   m = 1,   navsd = 0,   npts = 2001,   ntrk = 60 )  srchscs(poc, pod)  datumpmap(   xedg,   yedg,   datum = c("point", "line", "area", "corridor", "general"),   center = c(0, 0),   sigma = 1,   end = NULL,   nodes = 64,   wts = NULL )  optcrcsrch(sigma, W, effort)  opteffort(poc, area = NULL, W, effort, tol = 1e-14)

title: Search theory for search and rescue planning — ltrlrng
text: x Numeric vector: lateral ranges (distances track), sign. swpwdth(), strictly increasing abscissae, rmbl_ltrlrng object (p taken ). W Positive number: sweep width, distance unit grid effort (nautical miles, kilometres: one unit throughout). srchpod(), give effort area place coverage; default NULL. model ltrlrng() pswppod(): "invcube" (default), "definite" "mbeta". srchpod(): "random" (default), "definite", "invcube" "mbeta". m Number (0, 1]: M-Beta detection probability inside range. Default 1. navsd Non-negative number: standard deviation cross-track navigation error, units x. Default 0. p Numeric vector [0, 1]: lateral range curve x. coverage Non-negative numeric vector coverages (sweep width times track length area searched; 1 means effort equals area). Default NULL: W, effort area give , W * effort / area. Give one , . effort Non-negative number: total effort, track length (distance searchers travel searching, unit W). srchpod(), track length area, one number one per area (matrix laid like map area one); default NULL. area Positive numeric vector, one per cell: cell areas, square unit W. May NULL poc rmbl_datummap (cells' areas used). srchpod(), areas searched, map datumpmap() whose cell areas taken; default NULL. S Positive number: track spacing. npts, ntrk Whole numbers: quadrature points across one spacing (least 3, raised next odd number; default 2001) tracks side (least 1; default 60). poc Numeric vector matrix [0, 1], summing 1: probability area contains object (areas' shares, example consensus planners' scenarios). srchscs() opteffort() also probability map datumpmap(): cells areas, order .vector(map$poc). pod Numeric vector [0, 1], one per area, matrix one row per search one column per area. poc map, also matrix laid like map (one search, cell cell), srchpod() result one value per cell, opteffort() result (cells' PODs). xedg, yedg Strictly increasing numeric vectors: cell edges grid laid search area, east-west north-south, distance unit (seq(-5, 5, = 0.5): half-unit cells ten units). Cells may differ size. datum "point" (default), "line", "area", "corridor" "general". center Two numbers, x y grid's coordinates: datum point (example last known position), start line datum corner area datum. Default c(0, 0). sigma Positive number: standard deviation circular normal position error, distance unit (total probable error E 1.1774 sigma). Default 1. end Two numbers: end line datum opposite corner area datum; NULL point datum. nodes Whole number 2 1000: Gauss-Legendre nodes along line datum. Default 64. wts datum = "general": non-negative matrix cell weights, one row per y cell one column per x cell. tol Positive number: bisection tolerance log lambda.

1 of 3 rows beyond alpha = 0.001                         │ #> │                                                                       │ #> │   Largest distances first                                             │ #> │   row  distance  p_value  logpvalue  outlier                          │ #> │   ---  --------  -------  ---------  -------                          │ #> │     1     4.301  < 0.001     -9.250  TRUE                             │ #> │    32     2.900    0.015     -4.205  FALSE                            │ #> │    14     2.807    0.019     -3.940  FALSE                            │ #> │                                                                       │ #> │   1 of 3 rows lie beyond alpha = 0.001: row 1 (distance 4.3).         │ #> │                                                                       │ #> │   The distance measures how far a row is from the centre of the data  │ #> │   once the columns' scales and correlations are allowed for; the      │ #> │   p-value is from the chi-square distribution it would follow without │ #> │   outliers, and logpvalue its natural log, for rows far in the tail.  │ #> ╰───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # It is flagged, although both values lie inside the other rows' ranges. out$row[1] == 1 #> [1] TRUE range(df$height[-1]) #> [1] 147.8530 194.0162 range(df$weight[-1]) #> [1]  67.07546 101.82631  # A cluster of bad rows drags the mean toward itself; the median and # MAD move less, so the robust distance of such a row is the larger. bad <- df bad[2:21, ] <- list(height = 150, weight = 110) dclassical <- mahaoutl(bad, robust = FALSE) drobust <- mahaoutl(bad, robust = TRUE) dclassical$distance[dclassical$row == 2] < drobust$distance[drobust$row == 2] #> [1] TRUE  # A duplicated column has no distance defined, and is refused. dup <- df dup$height2 <- dup$height try(mahaoutl(dup)) #> Error : the columns are collinear, so no Mahalanobis distance is defined. Drop the redundant column(s) -- drpconst() and topcors() will find them.

title: Little's test for data missing completely at random — mcartst
code: set.seed(1) n <- 300 x <- stats::rnorm(n) y <- x + stats::rnorm(n)  # Missing completely at random: a coin flip decides, so the test # should not reject. mcar <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mcar$y[sample(n, 90)] <- NA mcartst(mcar) #> ╭── Little's MCAR test ────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Verdict        ✓ no departure from MCAR detected               │ #> │   Statistic      1.094                                           │ #> │   df             1                                               │ #> │   p-value        0.296                                           │ #> │   Patterns       2                                               │ #> │   Variables      2                                               │ #> │   Rows used      300                                             │ #> │   EM iterations  13                                              │ #> │                                                                  │ #> │   Not evidence OF MCAR: a large p-value is a failure to detect a │ #> │   departure, and this test has little power on small samples.    │ #> ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # Missing depending on the OTHER, observed variable: not MCAR, and # detectable, because the pattern's mean of x is shifted. mar <- data.frame(x = x, y = y) mar$y[x > 0.4] <- NA mcartst(mar) #> ╭── Little's MCAR test ────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Verdict        ✗ MCAR rejected: the missingness is related to the data │ #> │   Statistic      180.118                                                 │ #> │   df             1                                                       │ #> │   p-value        < 0.001                                                 │ #> │   Patterns       2                                                       │ #> │   Variables      2                                                       │ #> │   Rows used      300                                                     │ #> │   EM iterations  69                                                      │ #> │                                                                          │ #> │   Rows with different patterns of missing values have different means:   │ #> │   an analysis of the complete rows alone may be biased.                  │ #> ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # Complete data has one pattern and nothing to test. mcartst(data.frame(a = x, b = y))$df #> [1] 0  # A duplicated column makes the likelihood degenerate, and is refused. dup <- mcar dup$x2 <- dup$x try(mcartst(dup)) #> Error : the columns are collinear (or one is constant), so the multivariate normal likelihood Little's test is built on is degenerate. Drop the redundant column(s) first -- topcors() and drpconst() will find them.  # The EM estimates are the ML ones: with no missingness they are the # column means and the ML (1/n) covariance. fit <- mcartst(data.frame(a = x, b = y)) all.equal(fit$mu, c(mean(x), mean(y)), check.attributes = FALSE) #> [1] TRUE

code: chunks <- c("row1,row2", "row3,row4", "row5,row6", "row7,row8")  root <- mrkroot(chunks) root #> [1] "3b1537c90e21c2e66f341b946388abbb78bf249fb433f961fba223b67141be31"  # A single chunk's root is just its own leaf digest. mrkroot("only") == csha256(c(as.raw(0), charToRaw("only"))) #> [1] TRUE  # The leaves are the per-chunk digests, so a diff names the culprit. before <- mrklvs(chunks) after <- mrklvs(c(chunks[1:2], "row5,row6-EDITED", chunks[4])) which(before != after) #> [1] 3  # Prove chunk 3 belongs, without holding chunks 1, 2 or 4. pr <- mrkprf(chunks, 3) pr #> $sibling #> [1] "a1d2780e3c438372d14e12c01b280cf9be97a244adfa43671903812ca0deb88f" #> [2] "28ee5f4ac1a7a56c508b5f1b9cd5dd74abf929b3d0f2e5852280914ddef3cb88" #>  #> $side #> [1] "right" "left"  #>  #> $scheme #> [1] 2 #>  mrkvrf(chunks[3], pr, root) #> [1] TRUE  # The proof fails for a chunk that was not in the tree. mrkvrf("row5,row6-EDITED", pr, root) #> [1] FALSE  # Any change to any chunk changes the root. mrkroot(chunks) == mrkroot(c(chunks[1:3], "row7,row8 ")) #> [1] FALSE  # an odd count: the last node is promoted, so its proof has one step mrkprf(c("a", "b", "c"), 3) #> $sibling #> [1] "b137985ff484fb600db93107c77b0365c80d78f5b429ded0fd97361d077999eb" #>  #> $side #> [1] "left" #>  #> $scheme #> [1] 2 #>   # an index past the end is refused try(mrkprf(chunks, 5)) #> Error : `index` must be between 1 and the number of chunks  # a root pinned by 0.5.12 or earlier recomputes with scheme = 1, and its # proofs (which record no scheme) verify with a warning old <- mrkprf(chunks, 3, scheme = 1) old$scheme <- NULL withCallingHandlers(   mrkvrf(chunks[3], old, mrkroot(chunks, scheme = 1)),   warning = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")) #> [1] TRUE

title: Atmospheric dispersion: sigmas, plume rise, plume, puff, grid and particles — pgsig
text: pgsig(): Briggs (1973) fits Pasquill-Gifford dispersion coefficients stability class -F, rural sigmay = a_y x (1 + 0.0001 x)^(-1/2) (urban: 0.0004) sigmaz = a_z x (1 + b_z x)^(e_z). briggs(): buoyancy flux F = g v_s d^2 (T_s - T_a) / (4 T_s); final rise 21.425 F^(3/4) / u x_f = 49 F^(5/8) F < 55, else 38.71 F^(3/5) / u x_f = 119 F^(2/5), classes -D; 2.6 (F / (u s))^(1/3) s = g (dtheta/dz) / T_a x_f = 2.0715 u / sqrt(s) E F; transitional rise 1.6 F^(1/3) x^(2/3) / u x_f (EPA ISC3). gplume(): Q / (2 pi u sigmay sigmaz) exp(-y^2 / (2 sigmay^2)) V, V vertical term ground reflection , mixing lid, nimg pairs image terms. gspuff(): instantaneous release sigma_x = sigmay evaluated travel distance u t. advdif2d(): explicit upwind advection, central diffusion, forward Euler, zero boundaries. explicit scheme stable |u dt/dx| + |v dt/dy| + 2 (kx dt/dx^2 + ky dt/dy^2) <= 1 (von Neumann bound upwind advection forward-time centred-space diffusion); sum returned stabn stable. call outside bound run given: step split enough sub-steps smaller dt satisfy (reported substeps dt), warning, field solution physical time rather numerical explosion. separate cfl difn reported reference; 1 necessary, sufficient. lagrprt(): random walk x + u dt + sqrt(2 K dt) xi (Thomson 1987) optional counting grid. stability classes run "" (unstable, sunny light wind) "D" (neutral, overcast windy) "F" (stable, clear night light wind). Units SI: metres, seconds, kelvin; q g/s, gplume() returns g/m^3, mass g, gspuff() returns g/m^3. plume defined upwind source: receptor \(x \le 0\) gets 0. plume's h effective height, stack height plus rise briggs(). Every physical input checked: emission rates, masses, heights distances non-negative, wind speed, travel time grid steps positive, nimg whole number 1,000, stack hot air hotter (temperatures 150 refused probably Celsius), x0, y0 single numbers; release mixh warns, receptor ground lid (reflection terms give mirror values ). Unknown stability classes settings errors. Cost: gplume() gspuff() fast thousands receptors. advdif2d() R loop roughly 0.8 million cell updates second, grid models refuse run maxwork cell particle updates. particle walk reproducible seed touch R's random number stream. Progress bars shown interactive session.

title: Double machine learning for panels with fixed effects — plndml
text: model partially linear panel model $$Y_{} = \theta D_{} + g(X_{}) + \alpha_i + \gamma_t + \varepsilon_{}.$$ Following Clarke Polselli (2025), fixed effects removed within transformation (\(\tilde Y\), \(\tilde D\), \(\tilde X\)), \(\ell(\tilde X) = E(\tilde Y \mid \tilde X)\) \(m(\tilde X) = E(\tilde D \mid \tilde X)\) fitted learner \(K\) folds units (unit's periods one fold, unit's errors never help predict ). --fold residuals \(U = \tilde Y - \hat\ell\) \(V = \tilde D - \hat m\), partialling-estimator $$\hat\theta = \sum V U / \sum V^2,$$ solution Neyman-orthogonal score \((U - \theta V) V\) Chernozhukov et al. (2018). variance cluster-robust sandwich units, $$\hat V = \frac{G}{G - 1} \frac{\sum_g \big(\sum_{\g} V_i (U_i - \hat\theta V_i)\big)^2}{(\sum V^2)^2},$$ t \(G - 1\) degrees freedom. Folds drawn seed; nrep repeated splits combined median estimates variances plus squared deviations (Chernozhukov et al. 2018, section 3.4). Learners, base R: "lasso" (coordinate descent, penalty 5-fold cross-validation), "ridge" (penalty generalised cross-validation), "ols", function returning predictions (example random forest another package), called function(x_train, y_train, x_test). basis = "poly2" adds squares pairwise products covariates, built covariates observed demeaned, confounding combination removed exactly. demeaned features learners see: covariate fixed within unit absorbed unit effect carries information. learner given demeaned covariates (random forest, say) approximates nonlinear confounding less well; poly2 basis, basis user's covariates, remedy.

title: Plot a fitted Hawkes process — plothwk
text: Three views chwkfit() result events: "intensity" conditional intensity \(\lambda(t) = \nu(t) + \eta \sum_{t_j < t} g(t - t_j)\) window, baseline dashed events ticks along axis.
