title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
text: Estimates effect continuous exposure (treatment) outcome adjusting confounders, double machine learning recipe: part outcome exposure confounders predict removed models fitted folds data, effect slope left. answers questions “much asthma incidence rise per microgram NO2, holding income age structure fixed?”.

title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
code: plrcf(data, y, trt, covs, kfol = 5L, seed = 1L)

title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
text: data data frame one row per unit. y, trt Column names (single strings) outcome continuous treatment exposure; numeric. covs Column names confounders (one strings), numeric. Code categorical confounder indicator columns first. kfol Number cross-fitting folds, whole number least 2 (default 5). seed Seed fold assignment (default 1), estimate reproducible.

title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
text: list class c("rmbl_plr", "list") (print method shows box) ate (estimate \(\theta\): change outcome per unit treatment), se (sandwich standard error), n (complete rows used), kfol method (string naming estimator).

title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
text: partially linear model \(Y = \theta D + g(X) + U\), \(D = m(X) + V\) Chernozhukov et al. (2018, section 4.2), estimated DML2 cross-fitting recipe: sample split kfol folds; fold nuisances \(m\) \(g\) fitted folds predicted ; \(\hat\theta\) slope --fold outcome residuals --fold treatment residuals, $$\hat\theta = \sum_i \hat V_i \hat U_i / \sum_i \hat V_i^2,$$ sandwich standard error \(\sqrt{\sum_i \hat V_i^2 (\hat U_i - \hat\theta \hat V_i)^2} / \sum_i \hat V_i^2\). nuisances ordinary least squares covariates, right learner confounding approximately linear keeps estimator fully deterministic given seed; rmorie's morie_estimate_double_ml() offers richer learners can passed exprspplr estimator. fold's two least-squares fits computed normal equations covariates centred scaled full-sample moments (column space, fitted values lm.fit), solved Cholesky; fold whose cross-product poorly conditioned (reciprocal condition number 1e-5: collinear covariates constant column) uses lm.fit instead, whose pivoting drops redundant columns (coefficients count 0). n = 20000 fit takes milliseconds. bar stderr shows folds work slow enough need one (see blprog). Rows missing value named columns dropped first (n reports rows used). folds random permutation rep_len(1:kfol, n) drawn seed; R's random stream restored afterwards. Refusals: column name single string (several covs) data; non-numeric column (factor code); kfol whole number least 2; fewer 2 * kfol complete rows; treatment variation left covariates partialled .

title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
text: Chernozhukov, V., Chetverikov, D., Demirer, M., Duflo, E., Hansen, C., Newey, W. Robins, J. (2018). Double/debiased machine learning treatment structural parameters. Econometrics Journal 21(1), C1-C68.

title: Cross-fitted partially linear regression (double machine learning) — plrcf
code: set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(200), x2 = rnorm(200)) d$exposure <- 20 + 2 * d$x1 + rnorm(200) d$asthma <- 5 + 0.3 * d$exposure + d$x2 + rnorm(200) fit <- plrcf(d, "asthma", "exposure", c("x1", "x2")) fit$ate #> [1] 0.2536464  # A 95 percent normal confidence interval from the standard error. fit$ate + c(-1.96, 1.96) * fit$se #> [1] 0.1156209 0.3916718  # The fold split changes the estimate a little; ten folds instead of five. plrcf(d, "asthma", "exposure", c("x1", "x2"), kfol = 10, seed = 2)$ate #> [1] 0.2676102  # A text column is refused rather than read as codes. d$region <- sample(c("north", "south"), 200, replace = TRUE) try(plrcf(d, "asthma", "exposure", c("x1", "region"))) #> Error : column `region` must be numeric (a factor or character column is not a code)

A key built # from given seeds is not entered in the used-index record (it may have # signed elsewhere): it signs only after xmssregkey() vouches that it never # has. s1 <- paste(rep("11", 32), collapse = "") s2 <- paste(rep("22", 32), collapse = "") identical(pqckg(3, s1, s2)$root, pqckg(3, s1, s2)$root) #> [1] TRUE  # The height is limited to 16 (65,536 signatures). try(pqckg(height = 20)) #> Error : `height` must be a single integer between 1 and 16 options(op)

title: Bounds implied by rounding and suppression in a published table — pubbnd
text: Administrative releases rarely publish count observed. Statistics Canada rounds base (random rounding base 5 moves cell 4); provincial tables round nearest 5 10; cells disclosure limit printed "x", "<5" "..". text: x Published values: numeric vector, character vector (factor) suppressed cells appear one supmar "<k" limit k. rnd Numeric scalar, base release rounds (5, 10, ...), NULL (default) counts exact. rndkind "nearest" (printed value observed value rounded nearest multiple rnd, observed value lies within half base) "random" (Statistics Canada's random rounding, observed value lies within rounding - 1). suplim Numeric scalar NULL (default). cell printed suppressed explicit limit, smallest count published: cell lies [0, suplim - 1]. supmar Character vector strings mark suppressed cell, matched exactly trimming. Default c("x", "X", "s", "..", "F", "suppressed", "n/").

title: Bounds implied by rounding and suppression in a published table — pubbnd
text: data frame class c("rmbl_bounds", "data.frame"), one row per cell, value (numeric, published number, NA suppressed cell), lower upper (numeric, interval observed counts) status (character: "exact", "rounded", "suppressed", "missing" NA carried suppression mark). title: Bounds implied by rounding and suppression in a published table — pubbnd
text: published value \(v\) rounded base \(b\): rndkind = "nearest" observed count lies \([\max(0, v - b/2), v + b/2]\); "random" (unbiased random rounding, count moved one two neighbouring multiples) lies \([\max(0, v - (b - 1)), v + (b - 1)]\). bounds rounded whole numbers. suppressed cell lies \([0, k - 1]\), \(k\) "<k" suplim; rounding applied . Without rnd, published number taken exact (lower = upper = value). Text cells trimmed, thousands separators (commas) removed read numbers. missing value (NA) suppression mark gets status "missing" NA bounds. Errors: rnd one positive finite number; negative infinite count x; unknown rndkind; text cell neither number suppression mark (message lists cells); suppressed cell limit (neither "<k" suplim).

White: observed 2, published 1; Black: observed 1, published 2; Indigenous: observed 1, published 1. The observed counts match the published ones if the labels are permuted (White -> Black, Black -> White): the labels are attached to the wrong groups.

text: labels \(L_1, \dots, L_k\) code order, mechanism produces sequence \(M_1, \dots, M_k\) meaning “true group \(L_i\) seen \(M_i\)”. matches \(M_i =\) observed[L_i] \(\). five fixed mechanisms, \(k - 1\) rotations, two frequency orders cnts. obs identity mechanism reported matching. Errors: either argument unnamed; obs permutation labels vlabs.

title: Name the mechanical step that reproduces a label permutation — rlblfrns
code: # the OHRC 2023 case: alphabetical labels assigned to codes 1-4 vl <- c("1" = "White", "2" = "Black", "3" = "Other", "4" = "Unknown") obs <- c(White = "Black", Black = "Other", Other = "Unknown",          Unknown = "White") rlblfrns(vl, obs) #> ╭── Relabelling forensics ────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ #> │   Mechanisms tried  8                                                       │ #> │   Reproducing       3                                                       │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   The observed permutation is reproduced EXACTLY by: labels sorted          │ #> │   alphabetically, assigned by code position; labels sorted                  │ #> │   case-insensitively, assigned by code position; rotation by 1              │ #> │   position(s). No import routine (haven, foreign, pandas, pyreadstat)       │ #> │   reorders value labels; each carries them keyed by code. A transfer fault  │ #> │   does not select the sort order of the labels. The step that did this was  │ #> │   a positional relabel in the analysis, and it is reproducible from the     │ #> │   code book alone.                                                          │ #> │                                                                             │ #> │   Mechanism(s) reproducing the observed permutation:                        │ #> │   * labels sorted alphabetically, assigned by code position                 │ #> │       White -> Black, Black -> Other, Other -> Unknown, Unknown -> White    │ #> │   * labels sorted case-insensitively, assigned by code position             │ #> │       White -> Black, Black -> Other, Other -> Unknown, Unknown -> White    │ #> │   * rotation by 1 position(s)                                               │ #> │       White -> Black, Black -> Other, Other -> Unknown, Unknown -> White    │ #> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # a frequency-ordered relabel needs the counts obs2 <- c(White = "White", Black = "Other", Other = "Black",           Unknown = "Unknown") rf <- rlblfrns(vl, obs2, cnts = c(White = 50, Black = 10,                                              Other = 30, Unknown = 5)) rf$mechanism[rf$matches] #> [1] "labels ordered by decreasing frequency, assigned by code position"  # observed must be a permutation of the labels try(rlblfrns(vl, c(White = "Black"))) #> Error : rlblfrns: `obs` must be a permutation of the labels in `vlabs`

Their intervals      │ #> │   overlap, which alone does not mean they are the same: the difference │ #> │   has its own, narrower interval (svycmp() for survey domains).        │ #> │                                                                        │ #> │   Each rate is the count over the population times the base; the exact │ #> │   Poisson interval stays honest for small counts, where a normal one   │ #> │   does not.                                                            │ #> ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯  # a fractional count has no Poisson interval try(rtcalc(2.5, 1000)) #> Error : `count` must be whole numbers: a Poisson interval on a fractional count is not defined. code: f <- tempfile() writeLines("hello capsule", f) sha256file(f) #> [1] "55d6110230c260319d580bb6274db530b7e751c4f687fc00d0736ec531260a02"  # Deterministic: the same bytes always yield the same digest. identical(sha256file(f), sha256file(f)) #> [1] TRUE  # Any change to the file changes the digest (tamper-evidence). before <- sha256file(f) writeLines("hello capsule (edited)", f) after <- sha256file(f) before == after      # FALSE #> [1] FALSE  # Provenance pin: record a digest, verify it later. pinned <- sha256file(f) stopifnot(sha256file(f) == pinned)  # An empty file has the well-known empty-input digest. e <- tempfile() file.create(e) #> [1] TRUE sha256file(e) #> [1] "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"  # The file's bytes and the same bytes in memory hash alike. identical(sha256file(f), csha256(readBin(f, "raw", file.size(f)))) #> [1] TRUE  # A directory or a missing file is refused. try(sha256file(tempdir())) #> Error : sha256file: /tmp/RtmptAMHMc is not a file

title: Variance and standard deviation with the right correction, and why — sprd
text: \(n\) values \(x_i\) mean \(\bar x\): "sample" values drawn independently large population (process). \(s^2 = \sum (x_i - \bar x)^2 / (n - 1)\) unbiased population variance: \(n - 1\) (Bessel correction) makes measuring spread around mean sample , closer values population mean . standard error mean \(s / \sqrt n\). "census" every unit population observed (full count, complete administrative records) aim describe population: \(\sigma^2 = \sum (x_i - \bar x)^2 / n\), correction, \(\bar x\) population mean ; mean sampling error. population instead treated one realisation process (offences one year draw conditions city produce), use "sample". "finite" \(n\) units drawn without replacement \(N\): \(s^2\) (\(n - 1\)) unbiased population variance defined \(N - 1\), standard error mean \(\sqrt{(1 - n/N) s^2 / n}\); factor \(1 - n/N\) finite-population correction, negligible sampling fraction 5 percent. "auto" picks "sample" without N, "census" \(n = N\), "finite" \(n < N\). weights: frequency weights (value stands \(w_i\) identical observations) use \(\sum w - 1\); reliability sampling weights (value counts \(w_i\) times much) use \(\sum w - \sum w^2 / \sum w\), \(n - 1\) weights equal, standard error weighted mean sandwich \(\sqrt{\sum w_i^2 (x_i - \bar x_w)^2} / \sum w_i\). Survey weights complex design need design standard error (svydes).

Treatment taken staying . ctrl "notyet" (default) "never". meth "csa" (default) "wooldridge". cl Column name clusters (default unit), two column names two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), term small-sample factor dimension fewer clusters, t \(G - 1\) degrees freedom. composite cluster (district month, say) one column made interaction(). title: Effects of a policy adopted at different times — stgatt
text: Let cohort \(g\) units first treated period \(g\), \(C\) comparison units: never treated (control = "never"), yet treated period \(\max(t, g - 1)\) ("notyet", default). meth = "csa", $$ATT(g, t) = \big(\bar Y_{g,t} - \bar Y_{g,b}\big) - \big(\bar Y_{C,t} - \bar Y_{C,b}\big),$$ base period \(b = g - 1\) \(t \ge g\), \(b = t - 1\) ("varying" base package), pre-period ATT placebo one period. needs balanced panel. covs, parallel trends need hold conditionally , \(ATT(g, t)\) two-period estimator Sant'Anna Zhao (2020) cohort comparison units, covariates taken base period \(b\) (use covariates fixed treatment: one policy moves bad control). \(\Delta Y = Y_t - Y_b\), \(D\) cohort indicator, \(\hat m(X)\) least-squares fit \(\Delta Y\) \(X\) among comparison units \(\hat p(X)\) logistic propensity belonging cohort, $$\widehat{ATT}_{dr} = \frac{\sum D (\Delta Y - \hat m)}{\sum D} - \frac{\sum w (\Delta Y - \hat m)}{\sum w}, \quad w = \frac{\hat p (1 - D)}{1 - \hat p};$$ estmeth = "ipw" drops \(\hat m\) (normalised inverse probability weighting) "reg" drops weights (outcome regression). doubly robust form consistent either propensity outcome model right. Comparison units \(\hat p \ge 0.995\) trimmed, DRDID package . agree ::attgt() rounding error. meth = "wooldridge", regression outcome unit period effects indicator every treated cohort-period cell, never-treated (last-treated) units comparison, gives \(ATT(g, t)\) coefficient; without covariates equals imputation estimator. overall effect averages post-adoption \(ATT(g, t)\) weighted cohort size; event-time effect \(\theta(e)\) averages \(ATT(g, g + e)\) cohorts observed \(e\), weighted cohort size. Standard errors come cluster bootstrap: units (clusters) resampled replacement reps times everything recomputed; intervals normal bootstrap standard error.

code: df <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2, 2), age = c(30, -5, 40),                  start = c(1, 5, 3), end = c(2, 4, 9))  rules <- list(   rul("agenonnegative", function(v) v >= 0, col = "age"),   rul("idunique", function(v) !anyDuplicated(v), col = "id",        sev = "fatal"),   rul("datesordered", function(d) all(d$start <= d$end)) )  issues <- valrules(df, rules) names(issues) #> [1] "agenonnegative" "idunique"       "datesordered"    # A row-wise failure reports how many rows and which. issues$agenonnegative$n_failed #> [1] 1 issues$agenonnegative$rows #> [1] 2  # Clean data produces nothing. clean <- data.frame(id = 1:3, age = c(30, 31, 40), start = 1:3, end = 4:6) length(valrules(clean, rules)) #> [1] 0  # A rule for an absent column is skipped, not failed -- a missing # column is valsch()'s finding to report, not this one's. length(valrules(data.frame(id = 1:3), rules[1:2])) #> [1] 0  # A rule that errors is a failure, not a silent pass. broken <- list(rul("bad", function(v) stop("boom"), col = "age")) valrules(clean, broken)$bad$message #> [1] "Rule 'bad' failed (rule could not be evaluated: boom)"  # NA counts as a failure valrules(data.frame(age = c(30, NA)), rules[1])$agenonnegative$message #> [1] "Rule 'agenonnegative' failed (1 of 2 rows)"  # only rule() objects are accepted try(valrules(df, list(function(v) v >= 0))) #> Error : every element of `rules` must come from rul()

title: Validate a Data Frame Against a Provenance Schema — valsch
text: dfraw data frame validate. prov provenance list returned loadprov(), list(schema = infsch(df)). schema block may contain: expected_columns – required column names (character). missing one "fatal"; everything else "warning". structural_invariants – list min_data_rows max_data_rows (numbers rows). expected_value_sets – named list allowed values per column. expected_types – named character vector expected classes. integer, numeric double treated interchangeable, since re-release legitimately widens one another. numeric_ranges – named list c(min =, max =) bounds. max_missing_fraction – named numeric per-column ceilings share NA, 0 1. infsch() produces six data already trust.

title: Validate a Data Frame Against a Provenance Schema — valsch
text: named list issues; issue list severity ("fatal" "warning") human-readable message. names listed Details. zero-length list means data frame clean.

title: Validate a Data Frame Against a Provenance Schema — valsch
text: Every schema field optional checked present, schema written earlier version keeps working unchanged. STRUCTURAL check – names, types, bounds, value sets. tell column kept name, type range distribution moved; cpsdrft() answers . Rules particular data set (age must non-negative, two dates must ordered) belong rul() valrules(). checks, name issue one adds: missing expected_columns entry: missing_columns, "fatal"; fewer min_data_rows rows: row_count_low; max_data_rows rows: row_count_high; column whose class differs expected_types: type_<col>. integer, numeric double one family, character factor; non-missing values outside numeric_ranges (inclusive bounds; non-numeric columns skipped): range_<col>; share NA max_missing_fraction: missing_<col>; values expected_value_sets: unexpected_<col>. column check names data lack skipped check. expected_columns check reports column. "warning" except missing_columns. schema checked . empty schema (list()) gives one schema_empty warning. unknown field name within three edits known one (expected_colums) "fatal", otherwise ignored silently; unknown name warning. unknown structural invariant one edit, one swap neighbouring letters, away min_data_rows max_data_rows fatal; invariant names left alone. expected_dtypes accepted another name expected_types, synthetic_recipe known field checked . Errors: dfraw data frame; schema list. prov NULL schema returns empty list (use schval() make error).

title: Validate a Data Frame Against a Provenance Schema — valsch
code: prov <- list(schema = list(   expected_columns      = c("id", "year"),   structural_invariants = list(min_data_rows = 1),   expected_value_sets   = list(year = 2020:2025) )) df <- data.frame(id = 1:3, year = c(2020, 2021, 2030)) issues <- valsch(df, prov) names(issues) # flags the out-of-set year value #> [1] "unexpected_year"  # A column that silently changed type is caught. typed <- list(schema = list(expected_types = c(id = "integer"))) valsch(data.frame(id = c("1", "2")), typed)[[1]]$message #> [1] "Column 'id' is character, expected integer"  # So is a value outside its pinned range, and excess missingness. ranged <- list(schema = list(numeric_ranges = list(v = c(min = 0, max = 1)))) valsch(data.frame(v = c(0.5, 9)), ranged)[[1]]$message #> [1] "Column 'v' has 1 value(s) outside [0, 1]"  gappy <- list(schema = list(max_missing_fraction = c(v = 0.1))) valsch(data.frame(v = c(1, NA, NA, 4)), gappy)[[1]]$message #> [1] "Column 'v' is 50.0% missing, above the expected 10.0%"  # A clean frame produces nothing. length(valsch(data.frame(id = 1:3, year = 2021), prov)) #> [1] 0  # a misspelt schema field is fatal rather than silently ignored valsch(df, list(schema = list(expcol = "id")))[[1]] #> $severity #> [1] "warning" #>  #> $message #> [1] "schema field 'expcol' is not one valsch() uses: it was not checked" #>   # a schema inferred from trusted data, checked against a new release sch <- infsch(data.frame(id = 1:3, year = 2020:2022)) names(valsch(data.frame(id = 1:2), list(schema = sch))) #> [1] "missing_columns"  # the data must be a data frame try(valsch(list(id = 1), prov)) #> Error : valsch: `dfraw` must be a data frame

Entirely offline: nothing downloaded nothing written. Error: cpsdir one existing directory. Every problem failed row, error.

text: label \(l\) names(published) observed count \(n_l = \sum_i 1[x_i = l]\) (missing values excluded). counts match \(|n_l - p_l| \le\) tol every label. mismatch, 7 labels, function searches \(k!\) permutations labels (5040 \(k = 7\)) first non-identity one observed counts match published counts, names message. 7 labels search done permutation NULL. title: Verify recoded category counts against the counts a release published — vrfmrg
code: x <- c("White", "White", "Black", "Indigenous", "White", "Black") vrfmrg(x, c(White = 3, Black = 2, Indigenous = 1))$ok #> [1] TRUE  # swapped labels: the permutation that explains the counts is named r <- vrfmrg(x, c(White = 2, Black = 3, Indigenous = 1),                       strict = FALSE) r$permutation #>        White        Black   Indigenous  #>      "Black"      "White" "Indigenous"   # a release that rounds counts to the nearest 5 vrfmrg(rep(c("A", "B"), c(48, 21)), c(A = 50, B = 20),                  tol = 2)$ok #> [1] TRUE  # the default is to stop try(vrfmrg(x, c(White = 2, Black = 3, Indigenous = 1))) #> Error : vrfmrg: recoded counts do not match the published counts. White: observed 3, published 2; Black: observed 2, published 3; Indigenous: observed 1, published 1. The observed counts match the published ones if the labels are permuted (White -> Black, Black -> White): the labels are attached to the wrong groups.

text: poll "no2" "pm25" (also "PM2.5"), either case. y Outcome key concentration-response function; mortality outcomes count deaths, "chiast" incident cases. reg, years Labels report. demo Use synthetic demo data (TRUE FALSE). expcsv Path CSV exposure column micrograms per cubic metre, NAPS pull value column unit column (required value): row converted unit, NO2 ppb 1.88 micrograms per cubic metre per ppb (2021 conversion 25 C 1 atm), unit error. CSV demo data exposed rows ref: expoprev share expomean mean, Levin's formula diluted twice. expomean, expoprev Scalar inputs used neither demo expcsv given: mean exposure among exposed share population exposed. wrapper must never default one zero: prevalence zero silently zeroes burden, two required together. ref Counterfactual reference concentration; NULL takes pollutant's default (PM2.5 5.8, NO2 10; see crfpm25). brate Baseline outcome rate per 100,000 per year (unlike polbrdn, takes rate per person-year). basrateper denominator brate quoted per: 100,000 (default), 1 rate per person-year crude death rate 0.012. pop Population risk (persons). rare TRUE outcome really rarer one case per 100,000 per year. Without rate converts less assumption failure, also rate per person-year passed per 100,000 looks like (0.008 per person-year 800 per 100,000; 0.008 per 100,000 burden 100,000 times small). check converted rate, holds whatever basrateper . hirate TRUE outcome really common 10,000 per 100,000 year (population's -cause death rate ); without rate assumption failure. report result vrfpol() (list parts); anything else refused R error.

"ok" report also holds inputs (resolved exposure mean prevalence, rate per 100,000, population, reference rows dropped), assumptions (list assumption, ok, note) pipeline (crf, paf, pafci, displaced, burden equity, NULL without income data). polrpttxt(): single character string embedded newlines, ending STATUS: line ("ERROR:" message error report).

Empty cells missing-value tokens (NA, n/, null, - ...) dropped message; text number (detection-limit flag "<2") negative values stop run error report. gzip, bzip2 xz file decompressed; UTF-16 Latin-1 files decoded. income column, present numeric, gives equity stage (expconcidx). stages: crfpm25 crfno2; attrfrac CRF's interval; mortdisp removing excess exposure exposed population, \(\beta = \log(RR) / (\bar x - x_{ref})\); polbrdn. demo data 1,000 synthetic units lognormal exposures scale Toronto NO2 PM2.5 levels five income groups, drawn fixed seed (R's random stream restored).

Other pollutants reject. #>  #> Concentration-response #>   RR:       1.0286 #>   source:   Huangfu & Atkinson (2020) Environ Int 144:105998; WHO (2021) Global AQ Guidelines #>  #> Attributable fraction (PAF): 0.0273  (95% CI 0.0138 to 0.0534, from the risk's limits) #>  #> Mortality displaced #>   expected avoided deaths: 136.6 #>  #> Burden of pollution #>   attributable deaths:   136.7 #>  #> Equity analysis #>   concentration index: -0.0647 #>  #> STATUS: ok  # Scalar inputs: a city of 2.8 million at a PM2.5 mean of 9. s <- vrfpol(   "pm25",   expomean = 9,   expoprev = 1,   brate = 750,   pop = 2.8e6,   reg = "Toronto" ) s$pipeline$burden$attrcases #> [1] 510.8617 attr(s, "exitstat") #> [1] 0  # A CSV of measurements with an income column. f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") utils::write.csv(   data.frame(exposure = c(12, 18, 25, 31, 9), income = 1:5),   f,   row.names = FALSE ) vrfpol("no2", expcsv = f)$pipeline$equity$concidx #> [1] 0.02947368  # A rate per person-year passed as per 100,000 fails an assumption ... bad <- vrfpol("no2", expomean = 20, expoprev = 1, brate = 0.008) bad$status #> [1] "assumption_failure" # ... and an argument it cannot use is an error report, not an R error. vrfpol("no2")$error #> [1] "no exposure data: pass expcsv, or expomean and expoprev, or demo = TRUE"

title: Advance an XMSS key past a signature it made — xmssadv
code: # keep this example's op <- options(rmoriebricklayer.xmssidxfile = tempfile()) # one-time index record out of your configuration directory; leave the # default in use key <- pqckg(height = 2) s1 <- cpssign("manifest-1", key) key <- xmssadv(key, s1) key$next_index #> [1] 1 s2 <- cpssign("manifest-2", key) cpsvrf("manifest-2", s2, signpubkey(key)) #> [1] TRUE  # With the message, the signature is verified before the key advances. key <- xmssadv(key, s2, msg = "manifest-2") key$next_index #> [1] 2  # A key regenerated from seeds is unknown to the record until registered. s <- paste(rep("ab", 32), collapse = "") k2 <- pqckg(height = 1, skseed = s, pubseed = s, skprf = s) try(cpssign("m", k2)) #> Error : this XMSS key is not in the used-index record on this machine, and it claims never to have signed (next_index 0): it was generated elsewhere or from given seeds, or the record was deleted. If it has never signed, register it with xmssregkey(key); if it has, carry it forward with xmssadv(key, its_last_signature, message), or generate a new key with pqckg() invisible(xmssregkey(k2)) cpsvrf("m", cpssign("m", k2), signpubkey(k2)) #> [1] TRUE  # Reset a test key's entry so it may sign from index 0 again. xmssfgt(k2)  # A signature that is not an XMSS signature cannot advance a key. try(xmssadv(key, list())) #> Error : `sig` must be an XMSS signature from cpssign() (or the attestation, bundle or recode manifest that carries it) options(op)

title: rmoriebricklayer 1.0.0

Comparisons indgap() gives difference ratio reference group. dstntst() tests whether groups differ pooled (Cochran’s Q ²). ordcmp() compares rated scales, perceived mental health life satisfaction, whole distributions: probability higher rating, interval published limits. agestd() rategap() cover counts. stdprev() covers survey percentages. genexpo() exptrnd() cover intergenerational effects residential schools. trcind() maps indicator Call Action 19 (health gaps) Call 55 (children care, education, income) tables measure . trchlthgap() measures every gap non-Indigenous people one scale, “times worse”, intervals. Life expectancy infant mortality (tables 17-10-0160 17-10-0161) bundled . trccmpl() trcprog() track 94 Calls Action, Yellowhead Institute counts (Jewell Mosby).
